preamble: A palatalized bilabial nasal [mʲ] can lose its labial closure and keep only the palatal component, giving the palatal nasal [ɲ]. This is part of the wider pattern of labial palatalization, in which [pʲ bʲ mʲ] become [c ɟ ɲ]. It is well known from the Moldavian dialect of Romanian (miel 'lamb' pronounced [ɲʲel]) and from Lhasa Tibetan, where Written Tibetan my- clusters are pronounced with initial [ɲ].

examples.note: Labials before front vowels are palatalized and become [c ɟ ɲ]: copil 'child' [koˈkʲil], bine 'well' [ˈɡʲini], miel [ɲʲel].

examples.from: Written Tibetan smyon pa 'insane' (my- = palatalized m)
examples.note: The written my- onset is pronounced as a palatal nasal in the modern Lhasa language.
